problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 13 infrastructure projects to maximize overall community benefit.  
The profile of each project is as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.028, disruption index 0.074, allocation limits [0.079, 0.694]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.189, disruption index 0.218, allocation limits [0.006, 0.642]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.052, disruption index 0.014, allocation limits [0.062, 0.869]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.026, disruption index 0.277, allocation limits [0.053, 0.635]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.039, disruption index 0.200, allocation limits [0.073, 0.635]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.054, disruption index 0.279, allocation limits [0.083, 0.748]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.026, disruption index 0.251, allocation limits [0.008, 0.760]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.136, disruption index 0.146, allocation limits [0.022, 0.646]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.090, disruption index 0.195, allocation limits [0.052, 0.705]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.108, disruption index 0.115, allocation limits [0.010, 0.722]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.132, disruption index 0.226, allocation limits [0.023, 0.556]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.126, disruption index 0.268, allocation limits [0.039, 0.362]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.029, disruption index 0.248, allocation limits [0.019, 0.775]  

Each project must receive a share of the total budget within its specified allocation limits, and all shares must sum to one.  
To ensure timely completion, the group of quick-delivery projects, represented by Q = {D, G, I, J, L, M}, must collectively receive at least 0.506 of the total budget.  
At the same time, the overall disruption index for the portfolio must not exceed 0.228, and the total benefit score must be at least 0.058.  
Find the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
